item.title: Art as Resistance
item.description: The end of the world was not calm when the sixth seal was opened in the Book of Revelation. The sun turned black, the moon reddened, the heavens collapsed, and cities crumbled as humanity recoiled in fear. The Opening of the Sixth Seal, painted by Irish artist Francis Danby in 1826 and now held in the National Gallery of Ireland, displays this biblical scene in a vast, dramatic oil painting. item.title: Finding Permanence in the New Year: Advocating for Physical Media
item.description: While living in that liminal space between Christmas and New Years Eve, I tended towards what has taken over my free time since finishing finals: doomscrolling. Despite the feeling that I was wasting away, the shame of being unproductive, and above all not truly enjoying what I was doing with my time, the allure of that rhythmic scroll possessed me. That was until a revelation from my own feed—posts calling 2026 the year that we turn away from digital media in favour of the physical, woke me up.

item.description: As we begin implementing our New Year’s resolution, many turn to their closets to redefine themselves. item.title: Worn X Bred: “Worn by Locals, Bred in Ireland”
item.description: For all those who love local, Irish, interesting brands, Worn X Bred (WXB) is one to watch. item.description: DU Yoga Society Did last year’s exam stress get too much? Do you need an outlet other than doomscrolling?
